questions.label: Q1
questions.question: Have more than 180 days passed since the employment relationship ended?

questions.label: Q2
questions.question: Was the notice given because the employee had asserted, in good faith, claims arising from the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q3
questions.question: Has the notice period (from the notice to the end of the employment relationship) already ended?

questions.label: Q4
questions.question: Did the employee make the compensation claim pending (German: "Klage anhängig gemacht") within 180 days of the end of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q5
questions.question: Did the employee and the employer agree, after the notice, that the employment relationship would continue?

questions.label: Q6
questions.question: Was the employee, when notice was given, an elected employee representative on the staff council of the business or on a body linked to the business?

questions.label: Q7
questions.question: Did the employee ask the employer to state the reasons for the notice in writing?

questions.label: Q8
questions.question: Did the employer give the employee notice of termination of the employment relationship?

questions.label: Q9
questions.question: Did the employee lodge a written objection to the notice with the employer (German: "beim Kündigenden schriftlich Einsprache erheben") no later than the end of the notice period?

text:
Hello,

A friend keeps telling me I should take Erlenhof Services Ltd to court and ask for compensation. I haven't filed any claim, not with a court and not with the conciliation office, and I wanted to get proper advice from you before doing anything like that.

Some background. I'm a technician with Erlenhof in Biel/Bienne. I'm not on the staff committee or any other employee body, so I don't have anyone in the company who speaks up for me.

I've also never made any demands on them. I've never asked for a pay rise, never complained about overtime, never claimed anything. So whatever is going on, it isn't because I made a fuss about money.

What happened is this. On 21 July 2026 my manager, Noah Palmer, told me that from September I'm to work only night shifts at the Bienne site, and that my monthly pay of CHF 3,020 would be 'restructured'. When I said that nights are impossible for me because I look after my mother in the evenings, he just shrugged and said 'then think about whether this job is still right for you'. My colleague Emma Wälti was there and heard it.

To be clear, they have not given me notice. There's been no letter and nobody has said I'm dismissed. But it feels like they want me to give up and leave by myself.

Can they change my shifts and my pay like that? And is there any point in going to court when they haven't even fired me?

Thank you,
Leo Lüthi
Lindenweg 49, Biel/Bienne
